scope: The 9 catalogue papers eligible under the current 2026 Nature-family policy (retrospective ground truth). Facts (title/journal/epubdate/term hits) were retrieved live from PubMed on 2026-09-04; only vocabulary term names and metadata are stored - no abstract prose. Each entry records a rationale. Expected: the union of v2 PubMed pass 1 (AI x modality) and pass 2 (modality in title) must cover every eligible paper, because no single pass covers all nine.

fixtures.label: VirTues
fixtures.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales.
fixtures.rationale: Old PubMed pass-1 vocabulary missed this paper because no legacy modality phrase covers 'spatial proteomics'. The v2 expansion adds 'spatial proteomics' and 'multiplex'; pass 1 then fires on the indexed title/abstract and pass 2 fires because the title itself contains 'spatial proteomics'.

fixtures.label: Retina4IRD
fixtures.title: AI-based clinician decision support system for diagnosis of inherited retinal diseases: a multicenter, randomized trial.
fixtures.rationale: Retina4IRD was already rediscovered by the legacy query. Regression keeps it discoverable; the expanded AI terms (AI, vision transformer) make retrieval robust to title/abstract wording drift.

fixtures.label: AIOC
fixtures.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting fetal orofacial clefts and advancing medical education.
fixtures.rationale: Found by pass 1 because the abstract carries the modality term 'ultrasound' while the title only has the AI side. Regression guarantees the AI x modality pass keeps using the abstract, and that pass 2 alone (title modality) is not assumed sufficient for this entry.

fixtures.label: MouseMapper
fixtures.title: A deep-learning framework reveals whole-body perturbations at cell level.
fixtures.rationale: The known worst PubMed miss: the legacy query failed because the modality vocabulary did not include 'whole-body' and the title carries no microscopy word. v2 pass 2 (modality in title) catches it via the new 'whole-body' term; pass 1 still does not fire because PubMed-indexed text contains no expanded AI phrase (hyphenated 'deep-learning'). This entry proves why the two-pass union is required: neither pass alone covers all nine.

fixtures.label: MicroSplit
fixtures.title: Micro S plit  : semantic unmixing of fluorescent microscopy data.
fixtures.rationale: Legacy rediscovery case kept as regression. Note PubMed's indexed title contains odd spacing ('Micro S plit'), which is why matching relies on phrase/term presence rather than exact title text.

fixtures.label: BUSGen
fixtures.title: A foundation generative model for breast ultrasound image analysis.
fixtures.rationale: The known AI-vocabulary miss: the exact phrase 'foundation model' does not occur in the title ('foundation generative model'). The abstract does contain the expanded AI phrases, so pass 1 fires only because the AI vocabulary now includes generative/diffusion-style terms and because abstracts are used.

fixtures.label: Reti-Pioneer
fixtures.title: AI framework for multidisease detection via retinal imaging.
fixtures.rationale: The known AI-vocabulary miss for a title starting with 'AI': the standalone 'AI' term and the abstract-level 'foundation model(s)' phrases now satisfy the AI side of pass 1; retinal/fundus vocabulary covers the modality side.

fixtures.label: FluoResFM
fixtures.title: A foundation model for multi-task cross-distribution restoration of fluorescence microscopy images.
fixtures.rationale: Legacy rediscovery case kept as regression for the fluorescence-microscopy vocabulary.

fixtures.label: OVFM
fixtures.title: An ophthalmic video foundation model for surgical recognition and navigation with wet-lab porcine eye validation.
fixtures.rationale: The known modality-vocabulary miss: legacy terms had no way to flag ophthalmic surgical video. The v2 modality expansion adds 'ophthalmic' and 'surgical video'; the paper is then caught by both passes.
